  Readable gloss: "The noun ἱλαρότης denotes cheerfulness, gladness, or joyful disposition—the quality of being bright-spirited and generous-hearted. Romans 12:8 instructs that whoever shows mercy should do so "with cheerfulness" (ἐν ἱλαρότητι). The word emphasizes that acts of mercy and compassion should be performed gladly, not reluctantly or with resentment. The spirit in which ministry is done matters. Classical and Septuagintal usage associates ἱλαρότης with joy and gladness. Translations render it "cheerfulness" (English), "alegría" (Spanish), "joie" (French), "Froehlichkeit" (German), the glad-hearted quality that should characterize Christian service and mercy."
